nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type and let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence. The adjoint of the diagonal operator $D_a$ on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with coefficients $a$ is the diagonal operator with the conjugate coefficients $i \mapsto \overline{a_i}$.
nodes.title: Adjoint of a diagonal operator

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type, let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence and let $D_a$ be the diagonal operator on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with coefficients $a$. For every $x \in \ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \iota$, the $i$-th coordinate of $D_a x$ is $a_i x_i$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of a diagonal operator on ℓ²

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type, and for a bounded sequence $c : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ let $D_c$ be the diagonal operator on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with coefficients $c$. For bounded sequences $a, b : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$, we have $D_b \circ D_a = D_{ba}$, where $ba$ is the pointwise product $i \mapsto b_i a_i$.
nodes.title: Composition of diagonal operators

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and let $\iota$ be a type. The diagonal operator on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ whose coefficients all equal $1$ is the identity operator.
nodes.title: The diagonal operator with all coefficients one is the identity

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type, let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence and let $D_a$ be the diagonal operator on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with coefficients $a$. For $i \in \iota$ let $e_i \in \ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ be the sequence equal to $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere. Then for every $i \in \iota$ and every $c \in \mathbb{K}$ we have…
nodes.title: Diagonal operators on standard basis vectors

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type, and for a bounded sequence $c : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ let $D_c$ be the diagonal operator on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with coefficients $c$. For bounded sequences $a, b : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$, we have $D_a - D_b = D_{a - b}$, where $a - b$ is the sequence $i \mapsto a_i - b_i$.
nodes.title: Difference of diagonal operators

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type and let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence, that is, $\|a_i\| \le C$ for some real $C$ and all $i \in \iota$. The diagonal operator $D_a$ with coefficients $a$ is the bounded linear operator on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ that sends $x$ to the sequence $(a_i x_i)_{i \in \iota}$.
nodes.title: Diagonal operator on ℓ²

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type and let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence. For every $x \in \ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \iota$, the diagonal operator with coefficients $a$, regarded as a linear map, sends $x$ to a sequence whose $i$-th coordinate is $a_i x_i$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the diagonal linear map on ℓ²

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type and let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence. This is the diagonal operator on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with coefficients $a$, regarded as a $\mathbb{K}$-linear map $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K}) \to \ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ by forgetting its continuity.
nodes.title: Diagonal operator on ℓ² as a linear map

nodes.summary: Let $(b_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a Hilbert basis of an inner product space $H$ over $\mathbb{K}$ ($\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$), let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ satisfy $|a_i| \le C$ for all $i$, and let $D$ be the diagonal operator with coefficients $a$. Then $D b_j = a_j b_j$ for every $j \in \iota$.
nodes.title: Action of a diagonal operator on the basis

nodes.summary: Let $(b_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a Hilbert basis of an inner product space $H$ over $\mathbb{K}$ ($\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$), with inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ conjugate-linear in the first argument, and let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ satisfy $|a_i| \le C$ for all $i$. The diagonal operator $D$ with coefficients $a$ satisfies, for every $x \in H$,
nodes.title: Series formula for a diagonal operator

nodes.summary: Let $(b_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a Hilbert basis of an inner product space $H$ over $\mathbb{K}$ ($\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$), and let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ satisfy $|a_i| \le C$ for all $i$. Let $D_a$ be the diagonal operator with coefficients $a$, and let $D_{a^2}$ be the diagonal operator with coefficients $a_i^2$, which satisfy $|a_i^2| \le C^2$. Then $D_a(D_a x) = D_{a^2} x$ for every $x \in H$.
nodes.title: Square of a diagonal operator

nodes.summary: The bounded diagonal continuous linear map with coefficients `a` in the Hilbert basis `b`. Its uniform coefficient bound is part of the constructor.
nodes.title: Bounded diagonal operator on a Hilbert basis

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $\iota$ be a type and let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ be a bounded sequence. The diagonal operator on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ with coefficients $a$ is compact if and only if $a$ tends to $0$ along the cofinite filter on $\iota$, that is, for every $\varepsilon > 0$ only finitely many $i \in \iota$ satisfy $\|a_i\| \ge \varepsilon$.
nodes.title: Compact diagonal operators on ℓ²

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ be bounded, and let $D_a$ be the diagonal operator $x \mapsto (a_i x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$. Then $D_a$ is self-adjoint if and only if $\overline{a_i} = a_i$, that is, $a_i$ is real, for every $i \in \iota$.
nodes.title: Self-adjoint diagonal operators on $\ell^2$

nodes.title: Invertibility of a shifted diagonal operator

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. For every $c \in \mathbb{K}$, every $x \in \ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ and every $i \in \iota$, the $i$-th coordinate of $c x$ is $(c x)_i = c \, x_i$.
nodes.title: Scalar multiplication on $\ell^2$ is pointwise

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ is bounded, that is, $|a_i| \le C$ for some real $C$ and all $i$, then for every $x \in \ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$ the sequence $(a_i x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ lies in $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, that is, the family $(|a_i x_i|^2)_{i \in \iota}$ is summable.
nodes.title: Bounded multipliers preserve $\ell^2$

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ be bounded, and let $D_a$ be the diagonal operator $x \mapsto (a_i x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$. If $C \ge 0$ and $|a_i| \le C$ for every $i \in \iota$, then the operator norm satisfies $\|D_a\| \le C$.
nodes.title: Operator norm bound for diagonal operators

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ be bounded, and let $D_a$ be the diagonal operator $x \mapsto (a_i x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$. Then the operator norm of $D_a$ is $\|D_a\| = \sup_{i \in \iota} |a_i|$, where the supremum is taken to be $0$ when $\iota$ is empty.
nodes.title: Operator norm of a diagonal operator

nodes.summary: Let $\mathbb{K}$ be $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, let $a : \iota \to \mathbb{K}$ be bounded, and let $D_a$ be the diagonal operator $x \mapsto (a_i x_i)_{i \in \iota}$ on $\ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$, viewed as a linear map. If $C \ge 0$ and $|a_i| \le C$ for every $i \in \iota$, then $\|D_a x\| \le C \|x\|$ for every $x \in \ell^2(\iota, \mathbb{K})$.
nodes.title: Pointwise bound for diagonal operators

Analysis

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
